transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Ah, mighty Thor, welcome to Brokkr's forge. It's not often we see a god come through our doors. What brings the Thunderer here today?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Well, I've got a problem with this hammer you've got here.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Let me have a look... Mjölnir, of course. A fine piece of craftsmanship, fit for a god like yourself. What's troubling you about it?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: It's just not quite right. It feels off.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: I see. Well, the master smiths, Brokkr and the Sons of Ivaldi, are away deep in the mines at the moment. They'll not return for many weeks, I'm afraid. But, as it stands, all commissions from their workshops are considered fulfilled upon delivery to Asgard. Even a god must wait until the next forging-season and will need to pay anew for alterations or reforging.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Ah, I understand. But this is not a matter of personal preference or convenience. This hammer is a crucial weapon, and its defects cannot be ignored. I demand that it be reforged immediately upon my return to Asgard.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: I grasp the importance of Mjölnir, believe me. Yet my hands are tied by the agreements made. Perhaps, once Brokkr and the master smiths return, they can address your concerns at the next forging-season. Until then, is there anything else our forge can assist you with?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Fine, I'll just wait until the next forging-season. But remember, Brokkr, this hammer is of utmost significance. If it doesn't meet my standards, I won't hesitate to find another forge to do the job properly. Good day to you.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Understood, mighty Thor. Brokkr will indeed want to hear of your concerns upon his return. May your patience endure until then. Safe travels, and good day to you.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Good day to you.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Farewell, Thunderer. May the time pass swiftly until we see you again.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Yes, I suppose it will. Farewell, Brokkr. Until next time.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Until next time, Thor. May your journeys be safe and your hammer strike true. Farewell.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Thank you, Brokkr. I shall see you soon. Farewell.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Farewell, mighty Thor. Until we meet again.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Until then, Brokkr. Farewell.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Farewell, Thor. Safe travels.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Thank you, Brokkr. Farewell.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Safe paths to you, Thor. Until our next meeting.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Goodbye, Brokkr. Farewell.

Openness.behavioral_evidence: Thor focuses on the practical function of his hammer, showing limited interest in ideas beyond its utility.

Conscientiousness.behavioral_evidence: Thor emphasizes the importance of his hammer being repaired properly and is willing to wait for the next forging-season.

Extraversion.behavioral_evidence: Thor engages in direct communication and expresses his demands, but remains courteous throughout.

Agreeableness.behavioral_evidence: Thor shows some assertiveness in his demands yet ends the conversation politely, indicating mixed agreeableness.

Neuroticism.behavioral_evidence: Despite his dissatisfaction, Thor remains calm and agrees to wait for repairs, showing low emotional instability.
